title: Minimize SSE split-boundary races and ordered event flush
author: Marta Velasquez
release_notes: Fix: Resolve sporadic SSE reassembly races that produced partial/invalid JSON when chunk boundaries split tokens or `event:` lines; ensure deterministic ordering for interleaved function-call and normal events. Backwards-compatible parsing changes; no API break.
description: Motivation: Users reported rare but reproducible downstream failures when the OpenAI-compat SSE proxy emitted fragments that split inside critical token boundaries (eg. 'data: {' split across TCP frames) or where function-call sentinel events interleaved with regular events and were delivered out-of-order under high concurrency. These manifested as partial JSON parse errors, duplicated event delivery, or function-call arguments arriving before their leading sentinel. Root cause: the streaming parser allowed a tight race between chunk coalescing and event-window flush: a trailing partial 'data:' line could be considered complete by the socket layer, triggering a flush that the reassembly state machine interpreted as a terminal event even though the JSON body was incomplete. Approach: 1) Introduce a short, bounded reassembly window that holds non-terminal data fragments and performs a lightweight lookahead to determine whether a trailing fragment could be the prefix of a JSON object or an 'event:' header. 2) Add a brace-balance sentinel heuristic for JSON payloads: the parser keeps track of net braces and only emits a completed JSON event when braces are balanced and a following SST delimiter (blank line) or stream terminator is observed. 3) Implement ordered-event flush: each logical SSE event is assigned a monotonic stream-seq (local to the connection) at parse-time; the emitter guarantees in-order delivery semantics for events and function-call sentinels even when chunks are received out of order by the lower-level socket reassembly (this is enforced with a tiny per-connection queue that expires items after a configurable soft timeout to avoid head-of-line blocking). 4) Backcompat: default soft timeout is conservative (10ms) and can be tuned via redwood.openai_compat.sse.reassembly_window_ms. The parser preserves existing event prefixes and only changes when a potential split is detected, minimizing churn. Changeset summary: small state-machine changes in the SSE parser, a new reassembly queue and tests, and a minor shim in the OpenAI-compat adapter to propagate the config. Testing: added unit tests to cover partial 'data:' prefixes, fuzz-run reproductions with randomized chunk boundaries, integration test that simulates interleaved function_call + message events under a concurrency profile used in customer incident reproduction. Benchmarks indicate <1% median latency increase for streaming clients under normal load and significantly reduced incidence of parse errors under adversarial chunking. Rollout: feature-flagged behind openai_compat.sse.stable_reassembly (default on in main after this PR); we will monitor metrics (sse.parse_errors, sse.reassembly_time_ms, openai_compat.event_reorder_count) on the canary cluster for 72 hours before full cutover. Checklist: - [x] Repro-case unit and integration tests - [x] Fuzz harness added and CI integration - [x] Reviewer feedback addressed - [x] Bench numbers and dashboards updated - [x] Feature flag and runtime knobs added - [x] Release note prepared

2) compat: propagate sse.reassembly_window_ms config to adapter (M. Velasquez)
3) tests: add unit tests for split 'data:' prefixes and interleaved function_call events
4) ci: add fuzz harness job and small flake fix for SSE test harness
5) docs: docstring and console note about tuning knobs
files_changed: sse/parser.go - implement reassembly window and brace-balance heuristic; added 120 lines, removed 34 lines (snip: 'if isPotentialPrefix(chunk) { buffer.Push(chunk); continue }')
compat/openai_adapter.go - wire in reassembly_window_ms option and feature-flag; small shim to tag stream-seq on parse
sse/reassembly_queue.go - new file: lightweight ordered queue with soft timeout and metrics (added ~90 LOC)
sse/parser_test.go - new tests for boundary-split and interleaved events (includes fuzz harness hooks)
ci/fuzz/sse_fuzz.yml - add nightly fuzz job invoking randomized chunking scenarios
docs/openai_compat.md - note about tuning reassembly window and behavior
go.mod/go.sum - small dependency bump for testing lib
review_comments: Ava Chen: Can we avoid introducing head-of-line blocking with the reassembly queue? Suggest adding an expiry + immediate fallback path that emits an unbalanced JSON with a parse-error metric rather than stalling indefinitely.
Marta Velasquez: Addressed in commit 3: expiry implemented (default 10ms) and fallback emits parse-error metric sse.partial_emit with payload for post-mortem. Added comment to make behavior explicit.
Luis Martinez: The brace-count heuristic might fail for strings containing braces. Add string-aware counting or rely on a small JSON tokenizer.
Marta Velasquez: Switched to a lightweight tokenizer that tracks string state and escapes; now only counts braces outside strings. Tests added for edge cases like '\"{"' sequences.
Evan O'Neill: CI flaked on the new fuzz job; please make the harness deterministic in CI (seed) and limit runtime.
Marta Velasquez: CI change added: fuzz job now runs with a fixed seed in CI and is randomized nightly without a seed. Also added a 30s cap for CI runs.
ci_checks: fuzz-ci: initial run failed (flaky harness) -> rerun after harness fix: pass
benchmarks: perf regression check: pass (median latency delta < 1%)

Merged by Ava Chen using squash-and-merge. Commit message: 'fix(sse): reduce split-boundary races, ordered event flush, reassembly heuristics

Introduces reassembly window, brace-aware tokenizer, and ordered per-connection seq queue. Backcompat: configurable window and feature flag.'
